A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same TASO paper with complete, readable text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C. Pages 2–13 have identical extracted text and rendered images; differences are confined to page 1.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments on Qwen2.5-3B, LLaMA3.2-3B and DeBERTa-v3-base, plus ablations, runtime comparisons and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–5, Figures 2–4 and Appendices A–B.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain identical importance estimation, core-region identification, sequential structured LoRA pruning and sparsity-aware learning-rate scaling procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same GSM8K, BoolQ, WiC, ARC-e, ARC-c and GLUE tasks, including the same cross-task composition scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–2, the IMP/random-pruning comparison in Figure 3, and the dense-versus-pruned LoRA composition comparison in Table 4.

E3.justification: The development/test splits, evaluation metrics, model configurations, iterative training settings and Appendix C.1 learning rates are identical. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The learning-rate and core-region ablations, lottery-ticket/runtime analysis, cross-task composition study, and Appendix A–B importance-score and sparsity analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, independent repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Table 2's four iterative fine-tuning rounds are unchanged and are not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are retained. For example, Table 1 gives TASO average accuracies of 82.47 for Qwen2.5-3B and 71.82 for LLaMA3.2-3B in both versions; appendix results are also identical.

T1.justification: The importance definitions, binary masks, sparse-update equations and learning-rate scaling derivation in Sections 3–4 are identical. No mathematical correction or new proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about task-aligned redundancy removal and strong performance with approximately rank-1 LoRA parameter budgets. The new code announcement does not alter the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations in Section 5 and Appendices A–B are unchanged. Section 7 retains the limitation that evaluation covers standard NLP tasks and leaves applicability to other modalities unresolved.

D1.justification: v2 adds a TASO GitHub repository link with a code-availability statement in the abstract; v1 provides no code-access link. Existing implementation details, hardware disclosures and Appendix C settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the references retain the same cited works and positioning relative to LoRA, pruning and other parameter-efficient adaptation methods.

P1.justification: The abstract gains one code-availability sentence, and the arXiv version/date label is updated. The remaining prose, terminology and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added repository link produces limited abstract reflow and first-page spacing changes. All figures, tables, captions and page layouts from page 2 onward are visually identical.

improvement.justification: The explicit implementation link improves code discoverability and reproducibility information relative to v1. This is a limited documentation benefit: scientific evidence and appendices are unchanged, and the PDFs alone do not establish the repository's accessibility or completeness.
